messages:
sam: quick flag — noticed a bunch of 403s in prod when proxy sticky routing picks tenant from token vs X-Project header. affects customers using cross-project service accounts.
laura: ugh. reproduce steps?
ajay: saw that too during the canary. seems like when impersonation header present we prefer token.claims.project, which can be the target project not the origin project.
marta: which leads to quota attribution being wrong, right? billing shows tokens hitting target project instead of the org that owns the calling SA.
sam: exactly. failure mode: token is valid for project B but request intended to attribute to project A via X-Origin-Project. runtime routes to project B pool & enforces B's quota -> 403 if B exhausted. logs show route picked by `auth-proxy` decision.
laura: options: 1) force routing by explicit header `X-Origin-Project` if present; 2) prefer token claims always; 3) add a routing policy to prefer origin project for impersonation flows.
ajay: prefer-by-header feels simplest and explicit, but we need a fallback if header missing. i think priority: X-Origin-Project -> token.impersonator_project -> token.project.
marta: agree on priority but console UX also needs to show which field determined routing. ops teams keep asking why quotas are charged to different project. we should instrument a `routing_decision` tag in logs and in the dashboard.
sam: +1 on telemetry. can we add a small enum in traces: {HEADER, IMPOSTOR_CLAIM, TOKEN_CLAIM, FALLBACK_SERVICE} ? ops-bot: scheduled job created: auth-proxy/add-routing-decision-tag (#4532).
laura: edge case: delegated tokens where impersonator chain is longer: impersonator_project might be null but we have `delegation_chain=[sa1@A, sa2@B]`. which project to use? first non-null impersonator -> A?
ajay: propose rule: if delegation_chain present, use chain[0].project as origin. If header present override still.
marta: sounds good. but what about security — could a malicious client set X-Origin-Project to game billing? we need to validate header against token.allowed_origin list or require it only for internal trusted clients.
sam: yes validate: header only accepted if token has scope `allow_origin_override` OR token.subject belongs to our internal allowlist. otherwise ignore and log attempt.
laura: small implementation note: auth-proxy currently resolves project in two places — pre-routing (for pool selection) and later in quota evaluation. need consistent resolver in common lib to avoid drift.
ajay: i'll extract a single ProjectResolver util and add unit tests. also add an event metric `routing.decider` with tag=method so we can chart frequency of HEADER vs CLAIM resolution.
marta: for console, add a column on request inspector: "Resolved attribution" with value + reason tooltip. Useful for support.
sam: rollout plan: canary to sandbox, then opt-in flag per org, then default on after 2 weeks. must include telemetry check that HEADER usage < 0.1% for public tokens to detect abuse.
laura: test vectors? please add these: (1) normal token no header -> token.project, (2) impersonation token + delegation chain -> chain[0], (3) header present but token not allowlisted -> ignore, (4) header present and token allowlisted -> header wins.
ajay: adding tests + feature flag. i'll post PR with code and the test harness changes.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster will pick up auth-proxy image auth-proxy:v2.14.0-canary in ~30m.
marta: also add a brief note in runbook for oncall: how to interpret `routing_decision` and temporary mitigation (force project bind in console -> fallback pool).
sam: thanks — let's avoid surprise billing + 403 noise before wider rollout. will follow up with PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
laura: thanks, everyone.
thread_summary: Short thread about tenant/project affinity & sticky routing for auth proxy. Decided header-priority with validation, delegation-chain handling, unified resolver, telemetry tag, console UI change, and canary rollout plan.
